A private, bring-your-own-key AI chat client. Conversations stay in this app\'s storage on your device; answers come from the provider you configure.
This page describes what this app actually does with your data, based on the code in this build.

• Conversations, messages, and attachment references are stored in the app's own database.
• Attached images and text files are copied into the app's private files directory. Images are downscaled when they are added.
• Preferences such as theme, text size, voice, and the web search service are stored locally.
• API keys are stored in encrypted preferences backed by the Android keystore. Android backup is turned off for this app, so keys are not copied to a device backup.

When you send a message, the app sends it, the conversation context, your selected model, and your API key to the provider endpoint you configured. Attached images are sent as image data; attached text files are inlined into the message. Responses stream back. Inlet Chat has no server in between: the provider receives the request directly from your device, and that provider\'s own retention and training practices apply to it.

If you turn on web search, the search text is sent to the search service URL configured in Settings, and the pages it returns are fetched so their text can be used as context. That service and the fetched sites are third parties.

Voice input uses Android\'s speech recognition and voice output uses the system text-to-speech engine. Whether recognition happens on the device or through the device manufacturer\'s service depends on the recognizer your device provides, which this app does not control. Audio is only captured while the microphone button is in use.
This build contains no analytics, advertising, or crash-reporting SDK. The only network destinations are the provider endpoint, the configured search service, and pages reached through web search.

Deleting a conversation in History removes its messages and its copied attachment files from the device. Deleting a provider removes its stored key. Uninstalling the app removes its private storage. Data already sent to a third-party provider or search service is outside this app\'s control — use that provider\'s own deletion tools.

Inlet Chat has no model of its own. You supply credentials for a third-party AI provider, you are responsible for that key, and you must have the provider\'s permission to use it. Revoke the key at the provider if you stop using it.
Answers, model names, availability, and data handling are determined by the provider you configure. Inlet Chat does not control them and does not guarantee their output, accuracy, or uptime.
Usage is billed by your provider, not by this app. Inlet Chat makes no payments and sets no limits on your provider account. You are responsible for any charges your usage incurs.
Model output can be wrong, biased, or harmful. Do not rely on it for medical, legal, financial, or safety-critical decisions, and review anything you act on.
Search results come from third-party services and pages. They may be incomplete, out of date, or blocked, and the app may refuse to fetch some addresses. Verify important claims at the source.

Short answers for the things that usually go wrong. Inlet Chat has no account system, so everything below is something you configure yourself.

Open Settings → Provider → Add provider. Pick a preset to fill the name, endpoint, and a starting model, paste your API key, run Test connection, then Save. The first provider you save becomes the active one.
Where to get an API key
Sign in to your provider\'s developer console, create a key, and copy it. Keys are created and revoked on the provider\'s side, never in this app.
Test connection sends a single short message using the values currently in the form. It reports whether the endpoint, key, and model work before you save.
The provider refused the key. Check for a missing or extra character, that the key is still active, and that it belongs to the provider whose endpoint you entered. Create a new key if in doubt.

\"Unable to connect\" means the request never reached the provider — check your network and that the base URL is correct and starts with https://. \"Provider is unavailable\" or a timeout means the provider returned an error or did not answer in time; try again later. The base URL is the API root, usually ending in /v1.
Model not found or no model list
The model name is sent exactly as you type it. The model list comes from the provider and needs a working key and base URL; if it cannot load, type the model name your provider documents.

Voice output needs a text-to-speech engine installed — Google Speech Services is the usual one. Voice input needs the microphone permission and a working recognizer; some devices recognise speech only through a network service. If voice output is marked unavailable in Settings, the device has no engine.

Images and text files are copied into the app when added. Large images are downscaled, and unsupported file types are rejected. If an image is not recognised, try a PNG or JPEG. Text files are inlined into your message, so very long files make for very long requests.

Web search needs a search service URL in Settings → Web search and must be toggled on in the conversation. If Test search fails, the service is unreachable or blocked; try the default service or another instance. Answers still work without search.
